translations.answer: The matrix and CUDA demo in this thread were excluded; the original author found that `l/u` transitioned from double to float caused NaN/Inf, and Inf cast also led to NaN output in cuOSQP. Fixing the application to full float resolved the original issue. Therefore, it is recommended to check all `P/q/A/l/u` in the target dtype, especially the finite/inf encoding in bounds, before entering osqp_setup. The thread does not resolve differences between CPU/GPU and iteration speed, and full float cannot be considered as a complete performance fix.
translations.applicability: Applies to cuOSQP single-precision data path and MPC with infinite bounds; other GPU backends should verify their own type.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Compare `P/A`, set `P=0`, run 2×2/demo, check GPU configuration; finally, switch to full float data path.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Compare element-wise `P/q/A/l/u` values, finite state, and inf encoding between CPU/GPU in the final dtype; do not only compare the source double data.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Construct bounds using the target float type before entering cuOSQP, and explicitly check `isfinite`/allowed inf representation.
translations.details.environments.0: cuOSQP/OSQP C interface, CUDA 11.6, Visual Studio; MPC target 100 Hz; no release version.
translations.details.limits.0: Cannot attribute all GPU NaN to bounds cast; residual performance and solution difference from CPU/GPU are not closed.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author confirmed that full float modification resolved the original NaN; however, CPU/GPU solution difference and cuOSQP iteration speed still need to be investigated.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: What should be checked after replacing CPU OSQP with cuOSQP in the first iteration?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Perform finite check on all QP fields before real machine deployment; GPU solver returning NaN must reject control input and enter safe fallback.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The original author confirmed that the double→float conversion of `l/u` caused NaN/Inf and triggered NaN output.
translations.details.symptoms.0: CPU OSQP is normal, but cuOSQP returns NaN in the first iteration; official CUDA PCG demo is normal in the same application.
translations.media_summaries.0: The original post screenshot only shows cuOSQP returning NaN in the first iteration; the root cause is identified in subsequent text review of `l/u`, not from the screenshot.
